kind: Derived read-only audit of saved sampler and browser lifecycle
processSelection: The launched Node PID, plus visible /proc command lines containing the recovered chrome-linux64 directory. This is PID/path matching, not descendant traversal or proof of exclusive ownership.

browserLifecycle.sourceContract: Chromium launches once outside the mode loop. Each mode creates a fresh context. The per-mode finally awaits tracing.stop, swallowing trace-stop errors, then context.close. The outer finally awaits browser.close. Both actual trace archives are readable and renderer replacement is observed.

reparenting: Matching helpers with PPID1 are included; reparenting alone does not explain missing RSS. A fallback role label of browser does not mean a separate browser instance.
measurementLimitations: Matching can include another invocation using the same Chrome directory and miss nonmatching, unreadable or namespace-invisible processes.
Skipped /proc reads are not counted; sampler/services are omitted unless their command matches.
No PSS, per-PID cgroup identity, anonymous/file/shared RSS breakdown or complete process inventory was recorded.
RSS sums can double-count shared pages. Non-atomic five-second samples can miss peaks.
conclusion: The saved samples do not identify the owner of remaining cgroup anonymous memory, establish an application leak, or prove the readiness timeout cause. The later low-anonymous-memory cleanup observation is outside this saved sampler series.
